# Sourdough Bread

## Overview

My everyday loaf runs at 75% hydration with a 45-minute autolyse, then bakes in a preheated dutch oven at 250 C. It is forgiving enough for a weeknight and still gives an open crumb when I handle the dough gently.

## Steps

1. Mix 100 g active starter into 350 g water, then add 500 g strong white flour. Rest 45 minutes.
2. Add 10 g salt with a splash of water, squeeze it through, then fold the dough every 30 minutes for three sets.
3. Bulk ferment four to five hours at room temperature until it is jiggly and risen by about half.
4. Shape, place in a floured banneton, and cold proof 12 hours in the fridge.
5. Heat the dutch oven at 250 C for 45 minutes. Tip the loaf in, score it, lid on for 20 minutes.
6. Drop to 230 C and bake lid off for a 20-minute finish until deep brown. Cool one hour before cutting. The loaf keeps two days in a paper bag and freezes well sliced.

## Troubleshooting

A flat loaf is usually over-proofed, so shorten the bulk by an hour. A gummy crumb means I cut it too soon or the bake was short, so give it the full lid-off stage. A tight crumb instead of an open crumb means gentler folds and a little more water. A pale crust means the oven runs cool, so check the real temperature with a thermometer, mine reads 15 C low. A dense middle with a burnt bottom means the heat came from below, so raise the rack and slide a baking tray underneath. If the dough spreads instead of holding its shape, the starter was weak, so build it up with an extra feed before you bake again.
